accuracy.evidence: Period boundaries are rounded from the International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2023/09: Triassic 251.9 to 201.4 Ma, Jurassic 201.4 to about 145 Ma, Cretaceous about 145 to 66.0 Ma, so lengths of about 51, 56 and 79 million years. Dinosaur spans are rounded from the Natural History Museum Dino Directory and the Smithsonian: Coelophysis and Plateosaurus Late Triassic (about 215 to 201 Ma), Stegosaurus about 155 to 150 Ma and Allosaurus about 155 to 145 Ma (Late Jurassic, Morrison Formation), Brachiosaurus about 154 to 150 Ma, Tyrannosaurus rex and Triceratops about 68 to 66 Ma (Hell Creek Formation, end of the Cretaceous). The first dinosaurs date from about 230 Ma; Homo sapiens from about 300,000 years ago; the Chicxulub impact at 66 Ma ended the Mesozoic and birds are surviving dinosaurs. The Stegosaurus to T. rex gap (about 83 My) is greater than T. rex to today (about 66 to 67 My). The time line in the lab is drawn to one linear scale.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented children's ideas about deep time and dinosaurs (Trend 2001 on deep time; Catley and Novick on time lines; NHM and Smithsonian teaching notes): all dinosaurs lived together (step 5 predict, Stegosaurus and T. rex pair, p5, challenge tag met), the Jurassic is the longest or only dinosaur period because of the film (step 2 predict, tag famous), the order is Jurassic, Triassic, Cretaceous (step 1 predict, p1, tags swap and back), people lived with dinosaurs (a person bar, m4, tags cave and end), one dinosaur kind lasted the whole era (tag whole), and the era ended because dinosaurs got too big (tag big).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 559 Dinosaurs Were Real and 543 How Fossils Form do not mention the periods; 486 Ordering Events in Time and 734 Sequence Intervals of Time are about everyday events. This lab is built on one deep-time line drawn to scale from 252 million years ago to today: ordering period cards, measuring period lengths by tapping, dropping dinosaurs at a date that must fall in their period, measuring two gaps between marks, and judging pairs by whether their scaled time bars overlap.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children measure before being told: the Cretaceous block is visibly the widest, the orange Stegosaurus to T. rex bar comes out longer than the blue T. rex to today bar, and the five pairs are judged only from whether two bars overlap, with a dashed guide from each bar to the time line. Wrong drops name the period the dinosaur actually lived in with its dates, so the rule (each kind lived for a few million years in one period) is built from cases.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks which period came first with Jurassic tempting (most familiar name); the ordering disproves it. Step 2 asks which period was longest with Jurassic and 'all the same' tempting; measuring shows 51, 56 and 79 million years. Step 4 asks who lived closer in time to T. rex with Stegosaurus tempting; the two measured gaps show 83 against 67. Step 5 asks whether Stegosaurus could have fought T. rex with 'yes' tempting; the bars do not overlap.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor in the eight challenge questions has its own tag and message in meso_art.js WHY: jur, cret, swap, back, famous, same, trexjur, whole, met, tri, cave, end, big, notyet, first and before. In the lab, a wrong order names whether the period came earlier or later or is not the oldest, a wrong dinosaur drop names the period and dates it really lived in, measuring Stegosaurus straight to today is caught as the whole span, and each wrong pair judgement explains overlap or gap.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 3.0 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 8.0 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short ('Say T, J, C to remember it.'); the precise terms for the band (era, period, Mesozoic, Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous, million years ago, extinction) are in the key idea and the adult text, and the lab uses 'Mya' only next to a full 'millions of years ago' axis label.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs are the era, the order and lengths, the not-together idea, and the end of the era; the adult text gives curriculum links, what each of the five tasks shows with its numbers, and named mistakes; every hint points to a block, mark or bar in the lab.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, 2x) for every step at start, mid Show me and end, in light and dark themes, plus desktop at 1200 px. After the first pass the gap marks were made light in the dark theme, dinosaur labels were spread over three rows and the time line moved down so they clear the banner, the pair bars got a minimum width, a date label and a dashed guide to the time line, and the canvas was made taller on phones so the answer boxes clear the feedback box.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Place Triassic/Jurassic/Cretaceous, Measure the …, Put it in the …, Tap the Stegosaurus/T. rex/today mark, Could meet, Never met), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the period and its dates, the dinosaur placed and its dates, the gap measured, and the pair being judged.
